target.title: fix(feishu): pace outbound sends per target
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #14206.

Feishu outbound sends currently retry after the API returns rate-limit responses, but configured high-volume conversations can still burst several `im.message.create` / `im.message.reply` calls to the same Feishu target at once. That makes the first user-visible symptom a Feishu rate-limit error instead of a paced send queue.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an opt-in `channels.feishu.sendRateLimit.minIntervalMs` setting, with the same setting available under `channels.feishu.accounts.<id>.sendRateLimit.minIntervalMs` for per-account overrides. When configured, Feishu text, card, image, and file message sends are paced by account + receive id type + receive id. Different Feishu targets still send independently, and the default interval remains `0` so existing installs keep their current behavior unless they opt in.

## User Impact

Operators can set a small per-target send interval to avoid Feishu per-chat send bursts while keeping cross-chat throughput. Existing retry handling for Feishu 230020 / 11232 / 429 responses remains in place for server-side limits that still occur.

## Real Behavior Proof

Exact head after merging current `main`: `9378385f0745f93b109df44c541d999a5f018daf`.

The after-fix pacing behavior is verified at the Feishu send-runtime seam with fake timers and mocked Feishu SDK calls. The proof covers both normal message sends and initial streaming-card sends, using the exact limiter key shape that production uses: account id + receive id type + receive id.

Same-target configured pacing proof:

```text
config: sendRateLimit.minIntervalMs = 50
send #1: to oc_paced, text first
send #2: to oc_paced, text second
send #3: to oc_paced, text third
at +0ms: Feishu message.create called 1 time
at +49ms: Feishu message.create still called 1 time
at +50ms: Feishu message.create called 2 times
after final interval: Feishu message.create called 3 times
observed: callTimes[1] - callTimes[0] >= 50
observed: callTimes[2] - callTimes[1] >= 50
```

Distinct-target independence proof:

```text
config: sendRateLimit.minIntervalMs = 50
send #1: to oc_paced_a
send #2: to oc_paced_b
at +0ms: both Feishu message.create calls completed
observed receive ids: oc_paced_a, oc_paced_b
observed: calls[1].at - calls[0].at == 0
```

Streaming-card initial send proof:

```text
config: sendRateLimit.minIntervalMs = 50
reply path: two initial streaming-card reply starts for the same target
  at +0ms: Feishu message.reply called 1 time
  at +49ms: Feishu message.reply still called 1 time
  at +50ms: Feishu message.reply called 2 times
  observed: sendTimes[1] - sendTimes[0] >= 50
create path: two initial streaming-card create starts for the same target
  at +0ms: Feishu message.create called 1 time
  at +49ms: Feishu message.create still called 1 time
  at +50ms: Feishu message.create called 2 times
  observed: sendTimes[1] - sendTimes[0] >= 50
```

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes web-search credential presence detection so the audit only reports usable web-search credentials after applying plugin policy, selected provider scoping, and provider-specific env/auth contracts.

The earlier detector could treat credentials from blocked plugins or unrelated providers as web-search credentials. The latest fix also handles the Google plugin's split contracts: selecting `gemini` no longer counts `google-vertex` env such as `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` as a Gemini web-search key.

## Why This Change Was Made

Security/audit surfaces should reflect the selected web-search provider's actual runtime credential contract. Plugin manifests can contain multiple providers and env vars, so manifest env scanning must not flatten unrelated provider credentials into one web-search-positive result.

- Disabled, denied, or non-selected web-search plugins no longer make `web_search` look credentialed.
- Missing env-backed SecretRefs fail closed consistently.
- `tools.web.search.provider: "gemini"` with only `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` no longer reports Gemini web search as configured.
- `GEMINI_API_KEY` still reports Gemini web search as configured through the selected provider contract.

target.title: feat(xai): add native streaming TTS
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Add native xAI WebSocket streaming TTS through the existing `streamSynthesize` speech-provider contract.

This is separate from xAI realtime voice. It preserves the provider's existing buffered TTS, voice discovery, authentication, and telephony behavior.

## Behavior

- Streams from the canonical `wss://api.x.ai/v1/tts` endpoint.
- Rejects non-canonical streaming bases before bearer-authenticated WebSocket setup, including altered ports, credentials, paths, queries, and fragments.
- Sends ordered `text.delta` frames within xAI's 15,000-character limit, without splitting Unicode surrogate pairs, followed by `text.done`.
- Decodes `audio.delta`, completes on `audio.done`, and propagates server errors.
- Bounds encoded WebSocket frames and cumulative decoded audio.
- Refreshes the idle timeout for every audio chunk.
- Handles close-before-open, cancellation, completion, and repeated `release()` safely.
- Uses existing language, voice, codec, and speed controls; xAI defaults apply to sample rate and bit rate.

The existing Discord caller may deliberately fall back to buffered synthesis when a stream fails. Discord voice requests MP3 through a stream-only xAI provider override, including when a persona is active, while preserving the configured codec for buffered fallback. Other streaming callers retain all five xAI codecs.

## Evidence

Exact head: `f08d1fd20df3002d515869adf952529cce6986fd`

target.title: refactor(agents): converge CLI tool terminal reason onto run-termination
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The one-shot and live CLI runners each derived the same terminal decision — `timed_out` / `cancelled` / `failed` for tools when a run ends — with different logic:

- `src/agents/cli-runner/execute.ts` (one-shot) read the abort signal's lifecycle fields, then only recognized `FailoverError` timeouts; a `TimeoutError`-shaped or `AbortError`-shaped run error without an aborted signal classified as `failed`.
- `src/agents/cli-runner/claude-live-session.ts` (live) only sniffed error shape (`isTimeoutError`, `FailoverError` timeout, `AbortError` name) and never consulted the abort signal.

Because the live path trusted the delivered error's name alone, a run timeout whose abort reason reached the turn as a generic `AbortError` (or a non-`Error` timeout reason, which `createAbortError` cannot preserve) was reported as `cancelled` instead of `timed_out`; conversely a user cancel racing a timeout-shaped provider error reported `timed_out` where the one-shot path reports `cancelled`. Same decision, two encodings, observable drift — seam 3 of #104219.

## Why This Change Was Made

Converge the derivation onto one owner, per the #104219 change shape. `resolveCliToolTerminalReason` lives in `src/agents/run-termination.ts` — the module that already owns abort→stop-reason semantics (`resolveAgentRunAbortLifecycleFields`) — and encodes one rule: abort-signal lifecycle fields are authoritative when the signal has aborted; error shape (`isTimeoutError`, `FailoverError` timeout, `AbortError` name) classifies otherwise. Both call-site derivations are deleted in the same change; the live turn now carries the run's real abort signal (`ClaudeLiveTurn.abortSignal`, threaded in `createTurn`).

`terminalReason` feeds diagnostic events only (`tool.execution.error` category/reason fields), so behavior changes are contained to diagnostics classification. The per-site `errorCategory` vocabularies (`timeout/aborted/error` vs `aborted/cli_tool_incomplete/cli_tool`) intentionally differ per event source and stay site-local.

## User Impact

Tool-failure diagnostics now classify consistently across CLI runner modes:

- Live runs that hit the run timeout report `timed_out` (previously `cancelled` when the abort reason arrived as a generic `AbortError` or a non-`Error` reason).
- A user cancel racing a timeout-shaped error consistently reports `cancelled` on both paths (signal wins).
- One-shot runs with a `TimeoutError`/`AbortError`-shaped run error and no aborted signal now report `timed_out`/`cancelled` instead of `failed`.

No control-flow, retry, or delivery behavior changes.

## Evidence

- Drift sites and trace: old derivations at `execute.ts` (`resolveToolTerminalReason`) and `claude-live-session.ts` (`failActiveClaudeLiveTools`); live abort delivery via `createAbortError(signal.reason)` loses timeout identity for generic/non-`Error` reasons.
- Tests: table-driven matrix for `resolveCliToolTerminalReason` in `src/agents/run-termination.test.ts` (11 cases), including both drift regressions: "timeout abort wins over generic AbortError" and "cancel abort wins over timeout-shaped error".
- Local: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, `pnpm check:import-cycles` all exit 0; focused vitest green (`run-termination`, cli-runner suites — 270+ tests).
- Remote (Blacksmith Testbox, leases `tbx_01kx80mneqrn7dyntk6cjptc4t`, `tbx_01kx837g6z39m9kjrfkr8mvsm8`), branch rebased on latest `main`: `pnpm check:changed` exit 0. `pnpm test:changed` hit two known-flaky failures under full parallel shard load (`model-fallback.probe.test.ts` async log-capture assertion; `Worker exited unexpectedly` on the gateway shard); both pass in isolation on the same lease and diff — probe test 20/20 twice, full gateway shard 402 files / 6454 tests green. Neither touches this diff's surface.
- `git diff --numstat`: +43/−17 prod, +96 tests. Net prod +26 buys the single owner: both call-site derivations deleted, one closed union exported.

### Real behavior proof (ephemeral runtime)

Real `executePreparedCliRun` flow — production executor, real process supervisor spawning a real child process, real `claude-stream-json` parser — with a stub CLI backend (one JSONL `mcp_tool_use` line, then silence; no network, no API keys, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`). target.body:
Closes #103758

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where LINE groups configured with `requireMention: true` could not require a mention before non-text messages (image/video/audio/file) reached the agent. Any photo, video, voice clip, or file posted in such a group was always processed, regardless of whether the bot was actually mentioned, because LINE's Messaging API never attaches mention metadata to non-text messages and the mention-gate logic could not account for that.

Fixes an issue where operators of mention-gated LINE groups would see the bot react to every image/video/audio/file dropped in the chat, even when nobody addressed the bot, when they expected the same "must be mentioned" behavior that already applies to text messages (per #34438 / #35847).

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds two new **opt-in** LINE group config fields — `requireMentionForNonText` and `pendingMediaLimit` — so operators can explicitly turn on mention gating for non-text messages without changing default behavior for anyone else. Because LINE never reports a mention on the non-text message itself, a bounded per-group pending-media queue (default limit 3) retains the most recent skipped media until a later message in the same group is mentioned and fully processed, at which point the queued media is attached to that turn and the queue is cleared. This lets a user post a photo, then follow up with `@bot look at this`, and have the photo still reach the agent.

A prior attempt at the opt-in flag alone (#68197) went stale without merging and did not include the retention queue, which meant skipped media was simply dropped forever once a group opted in — this PR keeps the same opt-in, default-false posture that maintainers asked for on #68197, and adds the missing retention piece on top.

## User Impact

LINE operators can now set `channels.line.accounts.<id>.groups.<groupId>.requireMentionForNonText: true` (alongside `requireMention: true`) to require an `@mention` before non-text messages reach the agent, matching the existing text-message behavior. Skipped media isn't lost — up to `pendingMediaLimit` (default 3) recent items are retained per group and delivered alongside the next mentioned message. Existing configs are unaffected since both fields default to off/unset.

target.title: fix(perplexity): forward the execution abort signal to web search HTTP requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cancelling an agent run while a Perplexity `web_search` request is pending leaves that HTTP request running. The parent execution signal reaches the generic web-search runtime, but the Perplexity provider discards the execution context, so the request can remain open and eventually resolve after cancellation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward the `AbortSignal` from the tool execution context through the provider to the guarded endpoint helper (`withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint` / `withSelfHostedWebSearchEndpoint`), which already accepts a signal parameter.

The change does not alter Perplexity configuration, schemas, caching, timeouts, SSRF policy, provider ordering, or response formatting. A focused test verifies the signal handoff.

Sibling PRs applying the same pattern: SearXNG (#104216 by zhangguiiping-xydt, 🐚 platinum hermit), Brave (#104269), plus the companion PRs filed alongside this one. The Google/Gemini provider already forwards the signal and serves as the reference.

## User Impact

Cancelling a run now promptly cancels an in-flight Perplexity search instead of consuming network and server resources until the configured timeout or response. Normal completed searches and cached results are unchanged.

## Evidence

Focused suite passes on the rebased head, including the signal-forwarding test.

target.title: fix(gateway): add per-request cancellation to prevent late node.invoke dispatch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A pending plugin approval can execute dangerous `node.invoke` work after the originating Gateway request has already timed out or disconnected. This is a P1 security vulnerability (fixes #103980): the plugin approval window (120s default) exceeds the Gateway client timeout (30s default), creating a deterministic window where dangerous node commands can dispatch side effects after the caller has already observed failure.

Root cause: The TypeScript Gateway client removes its local waiter on timeout/abort but never signals cancellation to the server. The server-side WebSocket handler launches a detached promise without retaining per-request cancellation state. On persistent WebSocket connections, a client-local timeout does not close the socket, so the server never observes the cancellation boundary.

## Evidence

### Proof test results (18 tests across 3 environments)

```
$ pnpm vitest run src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.proof.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ PROOF-P2: pre-aborted signal immediately expires approval without waiting (54ms)
 ✓ PROOF-P1: abort during dispatch window is captured by listener guard (2ms)
 ✓ PROOF-P1: pre-aborted signal prevents any node registry invoke call (1ms)
 ✓ PROOF-race: approval cancellation wins when abort fires before decision (2ms)
 ✓ PROOF-normal: approval flow works correctly when no abort occurs (3ms)
 ✓ PROOF-deadline: request-level deadline cancels even without socket close (2ms)

 Test Files  3 passed (3) | Tests  18 passed (18) | Duration 8.56s
```

### Full test suite (57 tests)

```
$ pnpm vitest run src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.test.ts src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.proof.test.ts

 Test Files  6 passed (6) | Tests  57 passed (57) | Duration 10.25s
```

### Cancellation matrix

| Input form | Result |
|---|---|
| Approval completes before abort | `decision: "allow-once"` — normal flow |
| Abort fires before approval decision | `decision: null` (expired via `caller-aborted`) |
| Pre-aborted signal before `request()` | `decision: null` (immediate expiry, P2 fix) |
| Abort fires between check and invoke | `REQUEST_CANCELLED` (atomic guard, P1 fix) |
| Pre-aborted signal before `invokeNode()` | `REQUEST_CANCELLED` (no transport call) |
| Request deadline fires (persistent conn) | `decision: null` (deadline cancels even without socket close) |
| Normal flow without abortSignal | Unchanged behavior — backward compatible |

### Key proof: atomic dispatch guard prevents late side effects

The listener guard registers a one-shot `abort` listener that sets `cancelledBeforeDispatch = true` **before** any dispatch. A re-check after registration closes the race window. When the abort fires between the initial check and `nodeRegistry.invoke()`, the guard catches it and **the dangerous command never reaches the transport**:

```typescript
// P1 fix: atomic dispatch guard
let cancelledBeforeDispatch = false;
const onAbort = () => { cancelledBeforeDispatch = true; };
params.abortSignal?.addEventListener("abort", onAbort, { once: true });
try {
  if (params.abortSignal?.aborted || cancelledBeforeDispatch) {
    return { ok: false, code: "REQUEST_CANCELLED", ... };
  }
  // ... dispatch ...
} finally {
  params.abortSignal?.removeEventListener("abort", onAbort);
}
```

### Key proof: request-level deadline covers persistent connections

On persistent WebSocket connections where a client-local timeout (30s) does NOT close the socket, the server adds a request-level deadline timer using `MAX_PLUGIN_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_MS`. When this deadline fires, it aborts the per-request controller, expiring any pending approval even though the socket is still alive:

```typescript
// In message-handler.ts:
const requestDeadlineTimer = setTimeout(() => {
  cancelRequest("request-deadline-exceeded");
}, MAX_PLUGIN_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_MS);
```

### Key proof: pre-abort expiry prevents dangling approvals

AbortSignal does not replay past events. If `abortSignal.aborted` is already `true` when `addEventListener("abort")` is called, the listener never fires. The fix checks `abortSignal.aborted` before registering the listener and immediately expires the approval:

```typescript
// P2 fix: check before listener registration
if (params.abortSignal.aborted) {
  manager.expire(record.id, "caller-aborted");
  return { id: record.id, decision: null };
}
```

### Files changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.ts` | Atomic dispatch guard + pre-abort expiry + signal propagation |
| `src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.proof.test.ts` | 6 proof tests covering all cancellation scenarios |
| `src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.test.ts` | 3 new cancellation regression tests |
| `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/message-handler.ts` | Request-level deadline + cancelRequest() + .finally() cleanup |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/shared-types.ts` | `abortSignal` in `GatewayRequestHandlerOptions` |
| `src/gateway/server-methods.ts` | Forward `abortSignal` to handler invocation |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.ts` | Pass `abortSignal` to `applyPluginNodeInvokePolicy` |

---

## Summary

**Updated to address ClawSweeper review findings (Round 3):**
- ✅ [P1] Make cancellation atomic with node dispatch — abort listener guard + re-check after registration
- ✅ [P2] Check for already-aborted signal before awaiting approval — immediate expiry on pre-abort
- ✅ [P1] Cancel timed-out requests, not only closed sockets — request-level deadline timer
- ✅ [P1] Preserve request dispatch error handling — removed empty catch
- ✅ Forward `abortSignal` through `handleGatewayRequest` → `GatewayRequestHandlerOptions` → handler invocation
- ✅ Pass `abortSignal` from `node.invoke` handler to `applyPluginNodeInvokePolicy` to `createApprovalRuntime`
- ✅ Add `.finally()` cleanup for per-request socket close listener
- ✅ Add 6 proof tests + 3 regression tests

## Diagram

```
Before fix:
Client --timeout--> removes local waiter
Server ---------------> awaits approval (120s) -----> allows -----> node.invoke executes ❌

After fix:
Client --timeout/abort/close--> fires AbortSignal
```

target.title: fix(feishu): add 30 s request timeout to streaming-card API calls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where all six outbound CardKit and tenant-token requests in
`extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.ts` called `fetchWithSsrFGuard` without
a `timeoutMs` deadline. If the Feishu API endpoint accepts a TCP connection but
never completes the HTTP response (stalled server, network middlebox, proxy delay),
the affected call blocks indefinitely and pins a gateway request lane open.

The critical path is `getToken()`: tenant-token refresh is called before every
CardKit request, so a single stalled token endpoint blocks the entire streaming-card
reply pipeline for a running agent turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

`fetchWithSsrFGuard` exposes a top-level `timeoutMs` parameter that applies a hard
abort deadline to the underlying request. Adding `FEISHU_STREAMING_CARD_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000`
and wiring it to all six call sites in one constant covers every streaming-card path
without touching callers.

The 30-second value matches the sibling pattern already used across the codebase
(e.g. `extensions/googlechat/src/api.ts`, `extensions/google-meet/src/meet.ts`,
`extensions/mattermost/src/api.ts`).

`extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.ts` was checked and is not affected: its

through the caller's `init`, providing equivalent protection via a different mechanism.

target.title: fix(qa-lab): use truncateUtf16Safe for web snapshot maxChars cap
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `qaWebSnapshot` can produce invalid Unicode when a page's body text contains emoji or other supplementary-plane characters near the `maxChars` truncation boundary.

`qaWebSnapshot` caps the body text returned to QA scenarios with `text.slice(0, maxChars)`. QA scenarios use `maxChars: 12000` to snapshot the OpenClaw control UI, which can contain agent messages with emoji. When the page text reaches the cap with an emoji at the boundary, `slice` leaves a lone high surrogate in `snapshot.text` — which is then passed through `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty` and used in `text.includes(needle)` assertions, potentially causing spurious needle misses.

**Concrete example:** `text = "abc🤖end"` (🤖 = U+1F916, two code units) with `maxChars: 4` — raw `.slice(0, 4)` keeps `"abc" + U+D83E`, a lone high surrogate.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace `text.slice(0, maxChars)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(text, maxChars)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`, matching the established pattern used across `src/infra/restart-sentinel.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.ts`, and others. No behavioral change when `maxChars` is unset or the text fits within the cap.

## User Impact

**Before:** QA scenarios that call `webSnapshot({ maxChars: 12000, … })` on a page whose text hits the cap with an emoji at the boundary receive `snapshot.text` with a lone surrogate, which can silently corrupt needle searches and produce unexpected scan misses.

**After:** `snapshot.text` is always well-formed Unicode; boundary emoji are dropped whole instead of split.

## Evidence

- `extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.ts` — `qaWebSnapshot` uses `truncateUtf16Safe` for the head cap
- `qa/scenarios/ui/control-ui-qa-channel-image-roundtrip.yaml` — live QA scenario using `webSnapshot({ maxChars: 12000, … })` with emoji needle checks as canonical reachability
- `src/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime.ts` — exports `truncateUtf16Safe` as a proper SDK subpath for bundled plugins
- Regression: `extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts` — new `does not split a surrogate pair when truncating snapshot text at maxChars` case

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** `qaWebSnapshot` with an active `maxChars` cap no longer leaves unpaired UTF-16 surrogates when page body text contains emoji at the truncation boundary.
- **Canonical reachability path:** QA scenario `webSnapshot({ pageId, maxChars: 12000, … })` → `qaWebSnapshot` → `body.textContent()` → `truncateUtf16Safe(text, maxChars)` → `snapshot.text` → `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty(snapshot.text).includes(needle)` in scenario assertion.
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime; no real browser needed — `bodyLocator.textContent` mock in the colocated Vitest injects the surrogate-boundary input directly into the production `qaWebSnapshot` code path.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused `truncateUtf16Safe` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`; no provider/channel constraints — this is plugin-local web snapshot text handling.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (darwin 24.3.0), Node v22, branch `fix/qa-lab-web-snapshot-utf16`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
# 1. Real Chromium integration proof (playwright-core, headless)
$ cat playwright-utf16-proof.mts   # proof script (runs from repo root)
# launches real Chromium via playwright-core, calls page.setContent() with
# emoji content, reads body.textContent(), then shows raw .slice vs truncateUtf16Safe
$ pnpm exec tsx playwright-utf16-proof.mts

# 2. Regression suite
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ pnpm exec tsx playwright-utf16-proof.mts
=== real Chromium body.textContent() proof ===
body.textContent() length (code units): 8 | value: "abc🤖end"

raw .slice(0, 4):
  length: 4
  unpaired_surrogates: true
  hex: U+0061 U+0062 U+0063 U+D83E

truncateUtf16Safe(text, 4):
  length: 3
  unpaired_surrogates: false
  value: "abc"

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 RUN  v4.1.9 /Users/shen/Documents/GitHub/openclaw

 ✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts > qa web runtime > opens, interacts with, snapshots, and closes a page 78ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts > qa web runtime > launches an explicit Chromium executable override when configured 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts > qa web runtime > launches detected system Chromium without requiring branded Chrome 0ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts > qa web runtime > keeps an explicit browser channel request explicit 0ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts > qa web runtime > can close only selected page sessions 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts > qa web runtime > does not split a surrogate pair when truncating snapshot text at maxChars 0ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| extensions/qa-lab/src/web-runtime.test.ts > qa web runtime > caps oversized web runtime timeouts 1ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
   Start at  15:22:37
   Duration  535ms (transform 475ms, setup 321ms, import 44ms, tests 83ms, environment 0ms)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Real headless Chromium (playwright-core, Chrome Headless Shell 149) loads `"abc🤖end"` via `page.setContent()` and `body.textContent()` returns an 8-code-unit JS string. Raw `.slice(0, 4)` leaves `U+D83E` alone (`unpaired_surrogates: true`). `truncateUtf16Safe(text, 4)` returns `"abc"` (`unpaired_surrogates: false`). This is the same real Playwright `locator("body").textContent()` call path that `qaWebSnapshot` uses. Regression suite: 7/7 pass including the new surrogate-boundary test. The only failing CI shard (`src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts`) is pre-existing on `upstream/main` — reproduced locally without this patch.
- **What was not tested:** Full live QA E2E scenario (`control-ui-qa-channel-image-roundtrip`) with a real OpenClaw gateway rendering 12,000+ code units of agent output with emoji at the boundary. The Playwright `body.textContent()` → `truncateUtf16Safe` path is fully verified above.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor)
- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns
- Single commit on `upstream/main`; no bundled `scripts/` or release-script changes

## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
